regions.region: page 1 title, abstract, authors, keywords, and SI statement
regions.finding: The actual article title is recorded. The page states that SI is available online, but workspace mapping leaves SI association unestablished and no SI fact was imported.
Scheme 1 is an identity/example panel for naturally occurring axially chiral allenes, not a reaction scheme; no experiment was fabricated from the structures.

The Ogasawara/Hayashi Pd-catalyzed dienyl-bromide/malonate coupling was retained as a literature example with the printed 76% ee. The 7-step 94% ee and 15-step 90% ee route summaries lack experiment-level arrows/conditions here and remain coverage context rather than invented single reactions.

regions.region: page 1 lower-right Scheme 2 reported Landor synthesis
regions.finding: Five visible prior-literature arrows were retained separately: I→II alkylation, II→III asymmetric reduction, III→IV bromination, IV→V malonate substitution, and V→laballenic acid hydrolysis/decarboxylation. Missing yields/conditions remain explicit.

unresolved: The prior literature examples omit most experiment-level quantities and outcomes.
Scheme 2's displayed LiAlH4 and page-2 named carbohydrate-complex reduction description are both retained; their precise formulation is not restated.

regions.region: page 2 upper-left completion of Scheme 2 discussion
regions.finding: The cited Landor final product is described as very low ee with [α]D20 = −3.0. This supports the final prior-literature record and is not assigned as a current-paper result.
The R1←R2←R3←R4←R5←R6 diagram is retrosynthetic analysis and is classified as general_scheme; the forward experimental records are separate.

The 100 mmol ZnBr2/(R)-diphenylprolinol/TBS-propargyl ether/n-dodecanal allenylation followed by TBAF desilylation is one sequential preparation with a 48% combined yield and 98% ee. The two stages and temperature program are explicit in the record.
R6 mesylation followed by dimethyl-malonate substitution is retained as one sequential two-stage preparation with 70% combined yield and 98% ee; exact page-4 operations enrich this record.

regions.region: page 2 lower-right discussion of Scheme 4/5 transformations
regions.finding: Krapcho decarboxylation, DIBAL reduction, Wittig/hydrolysis homologation, and Ag2O oxidation are linked to their distinct Scheme 4/5 and experimental-section records rather than duplicated from prose.

unresolved: Equation 2 prints 2.0 equiv dimethyl malonate, whereas the detailed charge is 110 mmol for 50 mmol R6.

regions.finding: Three forward transformations are distinguished: R5→R4 Krapcho decarboxylation (73%, 98% ee), R4→R3 DIBAL reduction (76%), and sequential R3→IM1→R2 Wittig/hydrolysis homologation (86%). Exact unit operations are linked to pages 4–5.

regions.region: page 3 left-center Scheme 5 and preceding sentence
regions.finding: The source contains a direct conflict: Results-and-Discussion prints R1 as 1.0618 g/73%, while Scheme 5 prints 76%; both are retained, later reconciled only as an unresolved source discrepancy against the detailed 1.062 g/76% paragraph.
R1→R7 is a separate analytical methyl-ester preparation (68%, 98% ee), not part of the oxidation yield.
The 12% overall yield and 98% ee summarize the whole route; they are not assigned as a stage yield or a new experiment.

regions.region: page 3 lower-right General Methods and beginning of R6 procedure
regions.finding: General analytical/drying methods are context. The detailed R6 procedure begins here with vessel, argon, exact ZnBr2/prolinol/TBS ether/dodecanal/toluene quantities, room-temperature pre-stirs, and 130 °C start; it enriches Equation 1.

unresolved: The 73% versus 76% oxidation yield conflict remains unresolved.

regions.region: page 4 upper-left completion of R6 procedure

Mesylation and malonate substitution are recorded in operational order with all printed reagent/solvent quantities, 0 °C additions/hold, room-temperature anion formation, 10 h syringe-pump addition, 10.5 h total completion, workup, 11.683 g, 70% two-step yield, and 98% ee.
